headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in Saudi sofa factory fire
summary: Only one worker survived as doors were reportedly locked from the outside to avoid police detection of an illegal operation.
details: A devastating fire at a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has killed 16 Bangladeshi workers. Only one worker, Habibur Rahman, survived the blaze.
The sole survivor described a harrowing escape, explaining that he was at a nearby barbershop when the fire broke out around 1:30 PM.
Reports indicate the factory was operating illegally. A former worker claimed the doors were locked from the outside to prevent police from entering, trapping the workers inside.
Of the 16 victims, seven died from smoke inhalation, while others suffered severe burns. All victims' passports and documents were destroyed in the fire.
The majority of the victims were from Naogaon, with 13 from that district, and others from Natore and Rajshahi.
Families in Naogaon are in deep grief, with some victims having just recently married or planning to return home soon.
The Bangladesh government is coordinating with the Saudi embassy to repatriate the bodies of the deceased workers.
Local administrations in Naogaon are providing support to the families of the victims.

Reports indicate the factory was operating illegally. A former worker claimed the doors were locked from the outside to prevent police from entering, trapping the workers inside.

Of the 16 victims, seven died from smoke inhalation, while others suffered severe burns. All victims' passports and documents were destroyed in the fire.

The majority of the victims were from Naogaon, with 13 from that district, and others from Natore and Rajshahi.

headline_marked: Tk 1.21 crore [[robbed from Uttara fuel pump]]
headline: Tk 1.21 crore robbed from Uttara fuel pump
summary: Armed robbers stole the money from a fuel pump owned by the cousin of Tarique Rahman, with an employee injured during the attack.
details: A total of Tk 1.21 crore was robbed from the DL Petrol Pump in Uttara, Dhaka, on Sunday morning. The robbers, consisting of six to seven people, intercepted a covered van carrying the money to a bank.
The fuel pump is owned by Tasin Akter Huq, the cousin of Tarique Rahman. His mother, the late Khursheed Jahan Huq, was the elder sister of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia.

The incident occurred around 10:30 AM on Airport Road, in front of the Crown Plaza hotel. The robbers, arriving on three motorcycles, stopped the van and used pistols and a cleaver to steal the bag of cash.
Assistant Manager Mohammad Al Amin was hacked with a cleaver during the robbery. He was later rushed to the Bangladesh-Kuwait Friendship Hospital with the help of bystanders and other staff.
Police are investigating whether the robbers had prior knowledge of the the fuel pump's daily bank deposit schedule. Several suspects have already been identified by the police.
Airport Police Station has filed a case based on a case filed by the manager of the fuel pump, Abdul Karim. Efforts to be arrest the suspects are ongoing.
